results: 1. family history: mother, sister and grandmother affected - autosomal dominant pattern
2. genetic testing (targeted panel or exome): novel heterozygous NONSENSE variant in POU4F1; present in the symptomatic mother, sister and grandmother and absent in a healthy uncle
3. brain MRI: significant cerebellar atrophy with dilatation of the fourth ventricle
4. lumbar puncture / CSF: no oligoclonal bands - against multiple sclerosis
dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia caused by a heterozygous nonsense variant in POU4F1 (POU4F1 haploinsufficiency).

ALTERNATIVES:
1. Multiple system atrophy, cerebellar type (MSA-C) – would be sporadic and lacks the strong autosomal dominant family history with segregation of the variant.
2. Another genetic spinocerebellar ataxia not captured by the panel (e.g., SCA48 due to STUB1) – the segregation of the POU4F1 variant with disease makes this unlikely.
3. Immune-mediated cerebellar ataxia (e.g., paraneoplastic or anti-GAD associated) – absence of CSF oligoclonal bands and the clear autosomal dominant family history argue against this.
dx: Autosomal dominant cerebellar ataxia caused by a heterozygous nonsense variant in POU4F1 (POU4F1 haploinsufficiency).
